solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some show anger around champ

indicators.note: turned around, so the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone shows irritation while circling a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes WANG from the middle of 'show anger'; 'around' turns it to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to bite or chew noisily, and gnawing is a similar biting action.

clue.text: Administrative hub is under review, regularly lacking focus

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, at regular intervals, leaving the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: a focus is a centre of attention

explanation.surface: A head office under review is losing its sense of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly lacking' drops alternate letters of 'under review', keeping NERVE; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve centre is the control point of an organisation, where decisions are made.

clue.text: Scoundrel joins club — a means of achieving higher standing?

definitions.text: a means of achieving higher standing?

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club used for lofted shots
a heel is a cad or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain becomes a member of a society to climb socially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher standing' suggests social status, but it means literally standing taller.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge-heeled shoe has a solid raised sole that lifts the wearer up.

clue.text: The easiest way out of jumper, perhaps, is not to wriggle about

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is surround, the other pieces
to wriggle is to twist and squirm, so the letters of 'is not' are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a jumper is one example of a top, a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: Advice that the easy way out of a jumper is not to squirm around in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wriggle' turns IS NOT into STION, split S and TION to go 'about' the rest; 'jumper' is a garment, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft option is the least demanding choice available, the path of least resistance.

clue.text: Weather's certain to close in around six, see?

indicators.note: the outer word closes in round the inner letters

parts.note: certain means sure
VI is the Roman numeral six
v. is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A forecast that bad weather will close in around six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather's' is the verb plus 'is': to weather a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a crisis is to come through it intact, to live through it.

clue.text: Used when tack goes into foot, for example?

definitions.text: Used when tack goes into foot, for example?

parts.words: Used when tack goes into foot, for example?
parts.note: treading on a tack prompts swearing, and both tack and foot are themselves words of four letters

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: the curses yelled after standing on a drawing pin, and the fact that 'tack' and 'foot' each have four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swear words are commonly called by this name, after the length of many of them.

clue.text: Holding bottom of hat, too obviously

indicators.note: the first word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: overly means too much, excessively

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone grips the brim of a hat a little too conspicuously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too obviously' reads as one phrase, but 'too' is OVERLY, which holds T.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly and plainly, done in full view.

clue.text: Start popular movement that's lively, mostly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a trot is a brisk running pace

explanation.surface: Begin a well-liked dance that's fairly energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TROT to TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section or introduction, the start of a piece.

clue.text: August 27 — heading north to take in loch

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the letter
in a down clue, heading north means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the answer to clue 27 across, which is the word for black
L is an abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A date in August, 27th, with someone travelling north to a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August 27' looks like a date; 'August' is the adjective and 27 points to the answer EBON.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means grand and dignified, much like stately or aristocratic.

clue.text: Deter a tour abroad that caravans might have taken

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is put off by a foreign trip along a road once used by camel caravans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' is the anagram signal on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel caravans carried goods along established commercial paths such as the Silk Road.

clue.text: Go out to lunch to reflect

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, as is bats

explanation.surface: Someone takes a lunch break to have time to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out to lunch' reads as one phrase, but 'Go' is the definition and 'out to lunch' means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is to have a stab at it: an attempt or try.

clue.text: Servile types deported son — one from a Middle Eastern country

indicators.note: deported means sent away, so the letter for son is removed

parts.note: yes-men are fawning people who agree with everything the boss says
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fawning underlings send a son out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deported' removes S from YESMEN, leaving YEMEN, the country itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country on the Arabian Peninsula, and the adjective describes its people and things.

clue.text: Free time can start to subside, in general

indicators.note: these pieces are placed in the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
can is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: the start of the word means its first letter only

explanation.surface: Free time may begin to dwindle, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' looks like 'generally', but 'general' is LEE, which the other pieces go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To let loose is to release or set free something that was restrained.

clue.text: We stop to eat cooked food

indicators.note: cooked can mean falsified or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hungry travellers pull over for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it describes the food but rearranges the letters of 'We stop to eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet potato is an orange-fleshed tuber eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Pure water

definitions.meaning: as in 'a pure accident': nothing more than, sheer
a lake or pond, a body of water

explanation.surface: A label for clean drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'nothing but' (a mere child) and is also an old word for a lake.

clue.text: Basic flat is next to alleyway

parts.note: in northern English dialect an entry is a passage between houses
flat means even, which is level

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note that an apartment adjoins a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means even; in parts of England an alley between terraced houses is called an entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry-level products or jobs are the simplest, most elementary ones on offer.

clue.text: Manage to support extremity with large medical device

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the rest

parts.note: an end is an extremity
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large
to manage is to cope

explanation.surface: A hospital worker copes with propping up a limb using a big instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts COPE underneath END and OS in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a flexible tube with a camera used to look inside the body.

clue.text: Cover in rocks, initially showing disinterest

indicators.note: the cover is placed in the rocks

parts.note: stones are small rocks
a lid is a cover for a pot or box

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Something hidden in rocks shows signs of apathy from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' looks like part of the definition but supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolidness is a calm, unemotional impassivity, a lack of interest or feeling.

clue.text: Having reformatted hard drives, one spinning wildly

indicators.note: reformatting rearranges data on a disk, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: After wiping their computer's disks, someone spins out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard drives' reads as computer storage, but 'reformatted' shuffles only DRIVES into DERVIS, and 'hard' is H; 'wildly' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirling dervishes are Sufi worshippers who spin rapidly in their religious dance.

clue.text: Commends regiment that has captured large truck

indicators.note: the regiment captures, or encloses, the other letters

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service regiment of the British Army
a ute is an Australian name for a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A citation praises a regiment for seizing a big lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: UTE is short for utility vehicle, the Australian word for a pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to praise or pay tribute to them publicly.

clue.text: Tax record taken from subordinate

indicators.note: the record is removed from the subordinate

parts.note: a deputy is a second-in-command, a subordinate
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A tax receipt is confiscated from a junior employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' is a vinyl EP, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty is a levy charged on goods, as in customs duty or stamp duty.

clue.text: Departs for hotel in airport's final waiting area?

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another

parts.note: Heathrow is London's main airport
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A flight departure replaces a hotel stay in an airport's final departure lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial H of HEATHROW, the London airport, is swapped for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemned prisoners wait on death row for execution, a grim last waiting room, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Play diamonds and stick with ace

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
to ram is to thrust or stick something in
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A card player's tactic: lead diamonds and keep the ace in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a card move but is the definition; 'stick' means thrust, as a ram does, not keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, radio or screen.

clue.text: Figure on a small island drinks whisky

indicators.note: the outer letters drink in, or take inside, the inner letter

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
Whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A figure on a tiny island is knocking back whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure on' looks like a person on the island, but it is the definition: to expect.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure on something is to anticipate or expect it, to wait for it.

clue.text: At first, life is good in French capital

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A first-time philosophy that life is good, said in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French capital' looks like a phrase for Paris, but 'in French' goes with 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal.

clue.text: Just open a beer

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: An order to open a single bottle of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a jar' is a casual word for a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open, not quite shut, is described this way.

clue.text: Crazy Irish sailor turned fifty, touring Scottish island

indicators.note: going round the island, so the pieces surround it
turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
L is the Roman numeral fifty
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An Irish seaman celebrates turning fifty with a trip round a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned fifty' looks like a birthday, but 'turned' reverses only the sailor, and that reversed sailor plus fifty make the tour round the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrational means lacking reason or logic, much like mad or crazy.

clue.text: Soldier by river cases the opposition

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: the river encases, or surrounds, the word the

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A soldier near a river packs up the enemy forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opposition' looks like a whole definition, but 'the' goes inside ISIS, the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or opposite, the opposition of two ideas.

clue.text: Black book kept by one that's devious

indicators.note: the book is held inside the other letters
devious means wandering from a direct course, so the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A black book in the hands of a sneaky person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's devious' rearranges ONE into EON, which keeps B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for the dark colour of ebony wood.
